name: Vistra Corp.
key_signal: VST has pulled back ~28% from its 52-week high and trades below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages even as forward P/E (14.6x) sits far below trailing P/E (26.5x), implying the Street expects a sharp earnings inflection.
thesis: Vistra remains one of the purest public proxies for the AI/data-center power demand story, with 43% revenue growth, 26.6% operating margins, and a jaw-dropping 42.9% ROE. The stock's steep drawdown from $219 to $158 (52-week range low $132.66) has compressed forward P/E to 14.6x versus a trailing 26.5x, meaning the market is pricing in substantial near-term earnings growth that the 18 covering analysts collectively rate 'strong buy.' The 1-day pop of +1.8% and RSI near 52 (neutral, not oversold-exhausted or overbought) suggest the recent multi-month slide (mom_126d -11.9%) may be stabilizing rather than accelerating, giving a favorable entry point relative to where sentiment was a few months ago.
bear_case: The technical picture is genuinely bearish: price is below both the 50-day ($153.8) and 200-day ($165.5) moving averages with no golden cross, MACD histogram negative, and 126-day momentum down nearly 12%, all consistent with a stock still working through a valuation reset rather than bottoming. More concerning fundamentally, debt-to-equity of 367% and negative free cash flow (-$164M) show Vistra is heavily levered and currently cash-flow negative even as it's asked to fund the capex needed to capture the AI power-demand upside — if data-center demand growth disappoints or financing costs stay elevated (beta 1.41, 42.7% annualized vol), the deleveraging math gets much harder and the 'cheap forward multiple' thesis unravels quickly since it depends entirely on hitting aggressive forward estimates.
